visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A male speaker with short dark hair and glasses, wearing a black button-down shirt, stands in a studio setting. Behind him is a digital background of the Taipei 101 skyscraper at night, illuminated in blue. He gestures with his hands, holding a black pen. (2) The screen cuts to a digital overlay of a scientific research paper abstract titled 'A new rotation period and longitude system for Uranus.' The text is clearly legible against a white background. (3) The scene shifts to show a smooth, pale blue-green spherical image of the planet Uranus centered against a black void. The speaker remains in the bottom corner in a small inset. (4) A diagram appears showing eight planets of the solar system in a row, with their respective tilt angles and rotation directions labeled. The speaker returns to full frame briefly before another diagram shows Uranus's specific 97.77-degree axial tilt. (5) Three separate telescopic images of Uranus are displayed in a row, showing bright cyan patches on the planet's surface representing auroras. The speaker gestures toward these images to explain the findings.
